name: Anxiety
description: Feelings of worry, nervousness, or unease that may be accompanied by physical sensations such as restlessness, tension, and increased heart rate.

immediateActions.title: 4-7-8 Breathing Exercise
instructions: Sit comfortably with your back straight
Exhale completely through your mouth, making a whoosh sound
Close your mouth and inhale quietly through your nose to a mental count of 4
Hold your breath for a count of 7
Exhale completely through your mouth, making a whoosh sound to a count of 8
Repeat this cycle 4 times

immediateActions.title: Box Breathing Reset
instructions: Sit upright and place both feet flat on the floor
Exhale all the air out of your lungs slowly
Inhale through your nose for 4 slow counts
Hold your breath comfortably for 4 counts
Exhale through your mouth for 4 counts
Hold for 4 counts with empty lungs; repeat the box 5 times

immediateActions.title: 5-4-3-2-1 Grounding Technique
instructions: Take a slow, deep breath
Name 5 things you can see around you
Name 4 things you can physically feel (your feet on floor, clothes on skin)
Name 3 things you can hear right now
Name 2 things you can smell
Name 1 thing you can taste
Take another deep breath and notice how you feel

immediateActions.title: Progressive Muscle Relaxation
instructions: Find a comfortable position, lying down or sitting
Take 3 slow, deep breaths to begin
Starting with your toes: tense the muscles tightly for 5 seconds, then release for 10 seconds
Move up to your feet, calves, thighs, abdomen, chest, hands, arms, shoulders, neck, and face
For each group, tense for 5, release for 10
After completing all groups, take 2 minutes to notice the feeling of relaxation throughout your body

immediateActions.title: 5-Minute Sensory Reset
instructions: Close your eyes and take 3 deep centering breaths
Wash your hands with cool water and notice the temperature on your skin
Wrap both hands around a cold glass of water and hold it for 30 seconds
Open your eyes and slowly look around the room, noticing objects you have not paid attention to before
Eat one piece of food (fruit, chocolate, nut) as slowly as you can, chewing thoroughly and noticing flavour
Put your hand on your heart and take 3 more breaths before returning to your day

immediateActions.title: Tension Release Stretch Sequence
instructions: Stand up, feet hip-width apart, and roll your shoulders back 5 times then forward 5 times
Clasp hands behind your back, straighten arms, and lift gently away from your body for 3 deep breaths
Slowly tilt your head to the left, hold 3 breaths, then to the right, hold 3 breaths
Interlace fingers, turn palms up, and stretch arms overhead, leaning slightly left then right
Fold forward gently from the hips, letting arms hang heavy, and take 5 slow breaths
Roll up slowly one vertebra at a time and notice how your body feels

immediateActions.title: Worry Thought Reframing
instructions: Write down the specific worry thought that is on your mind
Ask yourself: What is the evidence this thought is true?
Ask yourself: What is the evidence this thought is NOT true?
What is the worst that could happen? Could I handle that?
What is a more balanced way to look at this situation?
Write down one small action you can take right now if appropriate

immediateActions.title: Stress Deconstruction List
instructions: Write down everything that currently feels stressful or overwhelming, one item per line
Read through your list and place a star next to items with a deadline within the next 24 hours
Place a circle next to items that are truly within your control right now
For starred+circled items, write ONE tiny next action you can take in the next 2 hours
For items you circled without a star, schedule one 15-minute slot later this week to address them
For items you cannot control, cross them off the list and say aloud: I release what I cannot change

immediateActions.title: Anxiety Labelling & Normalising
instructions: Say silently or on paper, finish these sentences: I am feeling _________ (name the exact feeling: nervous, exposed, judged, hot, tight)
This feeling makes me want to _________ (escape, hide, leave, freeze)
I have felt this way before and I got through it: TRUE / FALSE
The most likely outcome of this situation is _________ (not the worst case, the realistic case)
One kind thing I can tell myself right now is: _________
Now take 3 slow box breaths and choose your next small step

immediateActions.title: Conversation Safety Script
instructions: Before entering an anxiety-provoking situation, write down 3 safe, open-ended questions: How's your week been? Seen anything good lately? Working on anything fun?
Write down 2 safe responses for yourself: I agree completely / That sounds really interesting / Tell me more about that
Write 1 graceful exit line: It was so good catching up, I need to go grab a drink / check on something, I'll be around later!
Read through your script once and fold it away — just knowing it's there will reduce uncertainty
Remember: most people are thinking about themselves, not judging you — that is the quiet truth of most social moments

safetyGuidance: Anxiety is a common and treatable experience. Stress is a normal part of life, but when it becomes constant or overwhelming it can affect your health and wellbeing. If anxiety or stress is interfering with your sleep, relationships, work, or ability to enjoy life, consider reaching out to a mental health professional or your primary care provider. If you ever feel like you cannot keep yourself safe, please contact your local crisis line or emergency services immediately. You are not alone in this.
